incidents.observer_names: Georgian sources; Russian MFA officials citing Russian Ministry of Defense assessments
incidents.object_behavior: Alleged bombing of positions in Kodori Gorge; Georgian side alleged Russian planes violated airspace and bombed areas on October 28-29; Russian side categorically denied any Russian planes were involved
incidents.duration: October 28-29, 2001 — two-day period of alleged incidents
incidents.military_proximity: Gudauta military base (Russian), Kodori Gorge (active conflict zone involving Chechen fighters and Abkhaz forces)
incidents.notable_quotes: reports of planes in the area might as well have been about 'UFOs'; Moscow does not have the technical capability to determine whether there were foreign planes in the region; was not accusing anyone; any side had sent planes over Kodori; To posit that they could be UFOs would be humorous if it were not for the seriousness of the violations
incidents.cross_references: REF A: MOSCOW 13072; REF B: TBILISI 3087; MRN: 01 MOSCOW 13169
incidents.programs_mentioned: CIS Summit (November 30-December 1, Moscow); Boden Paper on Abkhazia; OSCE; USUN
incidents.people_mentioned: Deputy Foreign Minister Mamedov (Russian MFA); Ambassador Vershbow (US Ambassador to Moscow); MFA Georgia Desk Chief Tereoken (Russian MFA); Georgian Parliamentary Speaker Zurab Zvania; Russian Duma Speaker Gennadiy Seleznev; Defense Minister Sergey Ivanov (Russian); President Shevardnadze (Georgia); President Putin (Russia); George Krol (POLMINCOUNS, classifier of document); Georgian Polcouns Chkheidze; John Powers (Acting-Director, US Department of State, declassification authority)
incidents.key_takeaway: This document is not a genuine UAP incident report — it is a diplomatic cable about alleged Russian airspace violations over Georgia's Kodori Gorge in October 2001, in which a Russian MFA official sarcastically invoked the term 'UFOs' to deflect Georgian accusations, and the cable's title playfully adopted that framing despite the document containing zero actual UAP content.

incidents.location_raw: Papua New Guinea airspace, multiple locations including Wewak and vicinity of Angoram (approx. 4 deg S, 144 deg E)
incidents.observer_names: Air Niugini pilot (airborne, departing Wewak enroute Port Moresby); local residents at Wewak; various witnesses at multiple points around PNG; PNG National Intelligence Organization officer in Wewak
incidents.object_count: One aircraft observed moving north to south at 1900 local; six to eight aircraft traveling south to north at 2200 local; one radar contact flying south to north at high altitude and high speed
incidents.object_behavior: High-altitude, high-speed flight; one object traveling north to south at 1900 local; six to eight objects traveling south to north at 2200 local; radar contact traveling south to north at high altitude and high speed over Angoram
incidents.duration: Not specified; separate sightings at 1900 and 2200 local time
incidents.military_proximity: None specifically noted; query sent to USCINCPAC and 43rd Strategic Wing at Andersen AFB, Guam, suggesting concern about military aircraft proximity
incidents.notable_quotes: Pilot said his radar picked up aircraft flying south to north at high altitude and high speed when he was over Angoram (VIC 4 DEG S, 144 DEG E)
incidents.cross_references: 43rd Strategic Wing (43SW), Andersen AFB, Guam - telephone consultation referenced; USCINCPAC J3 and POLAD - action addressees; CSP-2025-00040 B-00002707027 (FOIA case reference)
incidents.people_mentioned: Gardner (cable signatory, likely Embassy Port Moresby officer); John Powers, Acting Director, US Department of State (release authority, signed 12/25/2026); Air Niugini pilot (unnamed); PNG National Intelligence Organization officer in Wewak (unnamed); Provincial Premier of Wewak area (unnamed); Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea (unnamed, was weekending in his electoral district)
incidents.key_takeaway: A January 1985 State Department cable documents Papua New Guinea's National Intelligence Organization formally inquiring about multiple UAP sightings over PNG on the night of January 24, 1985, including a corroborating radar contact by a commercial airline pilot, with the US Embassy denying any known B-52 or US aircraft presence and requesting confirmation from USCINCPAC and the 43rd Strategic Wing — notably using the term 'Unidentified Aerial Phenomena' in official correspondence four decades before that terminology became mainstream.

incidents.location_raw: Over Kazakhstan, approximately Latitude 45 North, Longitude 55 East
incidents.observer_names: Three American civilian pilots — Tajik Air Chief Pilot Ed Rhodes (American citizen) and two unnamed American pilot colleagues; former Pan Am pilots
incidents.object_behavior: Approached from over the eastern horizon at great speed and at much higher altitude than the aircraft. Maneuvered in circles, corkscrews, and executed 90-degree turns at rapid rates under very high G-forces. Eventually adopted a horizontal high-speed course and disappeared over the horizon. Contrails left behind at approximately 100,000 feet altitude reflected the maneuvering paths.
incidents.military_proximity: Airspace over Kazakhstan; no specific military installation proximity noted
incidents.notable_quotes: They described the light it emitted as having a 'bow wave' and as resembling a high-speed photo of a bullet in flight, in which a very small object gives off a much larger trailing wave of heat/light.; Rhodes noted that there is too little air/moisture at that extreme altitude to enable the creation of contrails by the propulsion mechanisms of ordinary aircraft which might be able to reach that height.; Rhodes expressed the opinion, which his crew seemed to support, that the object was extraterrestrial and under intelligent control.; Rhodes and his crew were adamant that they had seen thousands of 'falling stars' and other space junk entering the atmosphere in their years of flying passenger aircraft for PanAm. This, they insisted, was nothing like a meteor.
incidents.cross_references: Photos taken by Captain Rhodes with a pocket Olympus camera — to be forwarded to the Embassy and Tajikistan Desk (Lowry Taylor) if developed successfully; MRN: 94 DUSHANBE 259
incidents.people_mentioned: Ed Rhodes — Tajik Air Chief Pilot, American citizen (AMCIT), primary witness; Two unnamed American pilot colleagues of Rhodes; Lowry Taylor — Tajikistan Desk officer, US Department of State (recipient of photo copies); Escudero — signatory of the cable, presumably US Embassy Dushanbe officer; John Powers — Acting-Director, US Department of State (declassification authority, 2/25/2026)
incidents.key_takeaway: A January 31, 1994 US Embassy Dushanbe cable to the State Department, CIA, and DIA formally reports that three experienced American airline pilots flying a Boeing 747SP at 41,000 feet over Kazakhstan observed an unidentified object for approximately 40 minutes performing extreme maneuvers — circles, corkscrews, and 90-degree high-G turns — at an estimated altitude of 100,000 feet, which the pilots unanimously rejected as any known phenomenon and attributed to extraterrestrial intelligent control.

incidents.object_behavior: All 5 UAPs flew across the FMV screen/field of view (FOV). First UAP flew across FOV at 1514Z; 4 additional UAPs subsequently observed in FOV until 1934Z.

incidents.military_proximity: Active combat zone; Operation Inherent Resolve AOR; ISR mission supporting MAG unit conducting target development
incidents.notable_quotes: FROM 1514Z to 1934Z, [REDACTED] OBSERVED 5X UAP FLY ACROSS THE SCREEN.; AT 1514Z [REDACTED] OBSERVED A UAP WITH THE VISRECCE OF A POSSIBLE [REDACTED] MISSILE FLY ACROSS THE FOV IVO 38SMC53[redacted]96[redacted]; [REDACTED] PROCEEDED TO SEE 4X OTHER UAPS IN THEIR FOV UNTIL 1934Z. ALL 4X REMAINING UAP FIT CLOSER TO THE PROFILE OF POSSIBLE BIRDS.; DUST HINDERED MOST FMV COLLECTION OF THE GROUND.

incidents.location_raw: Wanaque Reservoir, New Jersey (Wanaque, Ringwood, West Milford, Paterson, Totowa, Wayne, Butler)
incidents.observer_names: Residents, motorists, municipal officials, police in prowl cars, reporters; calls came from multiple towns across North Jersey
incidents.object_behavior: Hovered over reservoir, made sharp dips and maneuvers, performed right angle turns, dove almost into reservoir, appeared stationary at high altitude, made stops at Lakeland Regional High School, Houdaille sand pit, overhead bridge on Ringwood Avenue, then disappeared. Reappeared at 2:15am over Wyckoff, then over Wanaque reservoir near Raymond Dam until 4:15am. Continued sightings Wednesday and Thursday night.

incidents.object_behavior: Hovered just above swamp 1,000-1,500 yards from dormitory; moved back and forth across ground; rose and descended; moved too fast for airplane; vertical and horizontal movements too rapid for conventional aircraft

incidents.object_behavior: Objects hovered at approximately 1500 feet altitude at negligible speed. A second object made contact with the distressed object for approximately two minutes then rose to original position. The distressed object ejected debris from one of its portholes. Objects then disappeared from view. Debris damaged the boat wheelhouse, spotlight, and klaxon, killed a dog and a sea gull.

incidents.location_raw: Kelso, Washington (crash site) and Tacoma, Washington
incidents.observer_names: Anonymous caller to Ted Morrello (United Press, Tacoma); Captain Robert G. Bjorning A-2 Officer McChord Field investigated crash
incidents.object_behavior: Anonymous phone calls to United Press wireman Ted Morrello claimed the B-25 was shot down, first by stating it was shot down generally, then specifying it was shot down from the air with a 20mm cannon. Army investigation found exhaust stack failure caused fire on left engine, left wing broke off taking tail with it. No sabotage indicated.

incidents.object_behavior: Object had crashed into ground at approximately 45 degree angle with left wing embedded in earth. Had slid 300-400 feet on impact. Was dented but generally intact. incidents.location_raw: 46 of 48 United States, including near Oak Ridge, Tennessee

incidents.object_behavior: Traveled in straight line at tremendously high altitudes and unbelievably tremendous speed. Could maintain altitude above ground contour possibly via radio altimeter. Could control speed and altitude. Approached US from north and returned northward over North Pole. None ever crashed or disintegrated over American soil. Reports of ability to turn in flight and return to launch base.

incidents.location_raw: Approximately one mile west of Merced, California (approximately 7 miles south of Castle Air Force Base)
incidents.observer_names: William H. Parrott, Major, USAF Active Reserve, pilot with approximately 2200 hours flying time, 12-A Langdon Villa, Merced, CA
incidents.object_behavior: First moving very slowly west or northwesterly; observer heard clicking noise for ~10 seconds before visually locating it; in view approximately 35 seconds; executed a 90-degree left turn; returned on southerly or southwesterly heading with louder clicking; clicking stopped when directly overhead and object was no longer visible; no whistle or roar; dog also reacted to object's direction throughout

incidents.key_takeaway: In July-August 1952, the FBI forwarded to Air Force Intelligence a witness report of UAP objects dropped from aircraft over a Canadian lake that then flew off at high speed, while also handling civilian correspondence claiming stolen flying saucer theories and a scientific article arguing flying saucers are optical/mirage phenomena.

incidents.date_raw: 16 January 1951, from 1915 hours (approximately 2145 hours per header)
incidents.date_normalized: 16 January 1951, from 1915 hours (approximately 2145 hours per header)
incidents.location_raw: Oak Ridge Area and vicinity, McGhee Tyson Airport area, Knoxville Tennessee; one object east, one west of McGhee Tyson Airport
incidents.observer_names: 663rd AC&W Squadron personnel (radar operators), AEC Patrol Personnel, Oak Ridge policemen, Captain I.O.M. Clevenger and Captain Wm. Aiken (controllers of 663rd); Major Raymond C. Care piloting AF 7177; F-82 crew
incidents.object_behavior: Eastern object: aircraft interception found it to be a star; spectral color change explained by atmospheric refraction. Western object: descended slowly over approximately one hour until disappearing behind trees. AEC-reported object: F-82 vectored south, no electronic or visual contact; AEC later reported it to be a star. Radar interference noted on AN/CPS-11 in approximate area of observed object; no interference on height finder AN/CPS-4

incidents.location_raw: Forest clearing near Hasselbach, Soviet zone of Germany, near Gleimershausen, Meiningen
incidents.observer_names: Oskar Linke, 48-year-old former mayor of Gleimershausen, and his 11-year-old stepdaughter Gabriele. Corroborating witnesses included a shepherd named Georg Derbst (about 1.5 miles away) and a sawmill watchman, both of whom saw what they thought was a low-flying comet.
incidents.object_behavior: Object was initially resting on the ground on the conning tower/cylinder struts. Two figures rushed back to it, climbed up the side of the conning tower, and disappeared inside. The cylinder then retracted into the object. The object rose slowly at first then ascended rapidly with a whistling sound, swerved toward a nearby village, and disappeared at terrific speed over hills and forests toward Stockheim. A circular depression was found in the ground afterward matching the shape of the conning tower.

incidents.object_behavior: Initially observed as slowly descending with a blue-orange funnel-shaped flame narrower at top than bottom; landed or near-landed in an arroyo; rose slowly straight up with light blue and orange flame from underside; roar changed from low to high frequency then ceased; object traveled southwest at low altitude (approximately 10-15 feet), cleared a dynamite shack by about three feet at high speed, then lifted and disappeared over Box Canyon or Six Mile Canyon Mountain; no flame, smoke, or noise during horizontal travel; emitted a sharp high-to-low whine as roar ended

incidents.location_raw: Socorro, New Mexico, approximately one mile south of Socorro in an isolated area near a dynamite shack, arroyo area off Old Rodeo Street
incidents.observer_names: Officer Lonnie Zamora, Socorro Police Department (primary witness); Sergeant M. S. Chavez, New Mexico State Police at Socorro (arrived after object departed, observed burning brush and tracks); Nep Lopez, radio operator (did not confirm visual)
incidents.object_behavior: Initially observed slowly descending with blue-orange flame underneath. Rose slowly straight up with loud roar starting low frequency then rising in pitch and volume. Flame came from underside at middle, approximately four-foot area, blue with orange at bottom. No smoke except dust. Rose to approximately 20-25 feet in about six seconds, then traveled southwest in a straight line at 10-15 feet altitude, cleared dynamite shack by about three feet, accelerated rapidly, shrank in apparent size quickly, cleared Box Canyon or Six Mile Canyon Mountain and disappeared. No flame, smoke, or noise during horizontal travel. Roar ended with high-to-low whine lasting about one second then complete silence.
